content_of_post_to_answer: Why do readers always have positive thinking?
answer: Readers do not always have positive thinking; many are drawn to books because reading creates distance from immediate problems and gives the mind a space to process them. A good reader often develops optimism not by ignoring reality, but by seeing more possibilities through different perspectives. The deeper shift is that reading can turn suffering into understanding. Positive thinking is often not a personality trait—it is a result of learning to interpret experiences differently.
